words.sentence: The tapir used its short, flexible snout to pluck leaves from low-hanging branches near the river's edge.
Resembling a horse with zebra-striped legs, the okapi is the giraffe's only living relative and was unknown to science until 1901.
The binturong hung by its prehensile tail in the canopy, filling the air around it with an inexplicable scent of warm popcorn.
When the pangolin sensed danger, it curled into a tight ball, its overlapping keratin scales forming a near-impenetrable armour.
The capybara waded into the river with calm authority — at 70 kilograms, it is the world's largest living rodent.
The dominant mandrill's face blazed with ridged blue and scarlet colouring, a signal of rank no other animal in the troop could ignore.
Unlike most salamanders, the axolotl never undergoes metamorphosis — it keeps its feathery external gills and lives its entire life underwater.
The fennec's oversized ears are not just for hearing — they radiate body heat, keeping the animal cool across the Saharan nights it hunts through.
The fossa looks like a small cougar, but it is more closely related to the mongoose — Madagascar's largest predator evolved in near-total isolation.
The aardvark sealed its nostrils against the dust and drove its sticky tongue 30 centimetres into the termite mound.
